oracle.invariant: No two encryption invocations may share both effective key bytes and nonce bytes.
oracle.observation_source: Nonce prefix captured from actual encryption helper output.
oracle.key_handling: Test-only exact key bytes retained in-memory as a map key; never logged or serialized.
non_claims: This corpus does not prove nonce uniqueness for executions it does not exercise.
Legacy witnesses are expected to reproduce the documented defect and are not security-passing assertions.
Runtime strict-path remediation must add opposite-expectation tests before this becomes a release gate.

scenarios.stimulus: Invoke packet encryption twice with one key and distinct source IDs whose first six bytes, payload type, epoch, and sequence match; then repeat nonce bytes under a different key.
scenarios.expected: The oracle flags the second same-key pair and accepts the distinct-key positive control.

scenarios.stimulus: Use source bytes 1122334455660088, valid WisdomVector packet type 0x00, epoch 0x88, packet sequence 0x00030201 and fragment thought ID 0x0201/index 3 under the same test key.
scenarios.expected: Packet and fragment helpers produce the same nonce; oracle flags the repeated same-key pair; equal-length ciphertexts expose plaintext XOR.

scenarios.stimulus: Encrypt fragments whose packet sequences differ by 65536 but whose thought_id values match, under the same key/source/index.
scenarios.expected: The actual helper outputs repeat the nonce and expose the ciphertext XOR relation.

scenarios.stimulus: Encrypt an MTU-sized LoRa fragment with the legacy per-fragment AEAD wrapper.

qualification_targets.legacy_witnesses: 100% of registered legacy witnesses reproduced for their intended reason
